Kasturba Health Society Observes a Month-long Special Campaign 5.0
Monday, 27 October 2025
2010 Hits
Kasturba Health Society, Sevagram observes a month-long Special Campaign – Manthan – from 2nd to 31st October 2025 across the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (MGIMS), Kasturba Hospital, Kasturba Nursing College, Kasturba Nursing School, and its community centres and adopted villages. The theme of the Special Campaign is to institutionalize Swachhata and minimize pendency. In alignment with the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare’s initiative, faculty, staff, students, and local communities participated in promoting swachhata, strengthening record management practices, and ensuring efficient and cleaner workspaces.
The preparatory activities undertaken prior to the campaign involved identification of pending files, redundant materials, and cleanliness priority locations. These initiatives encompassed Swachhata Abhiyaan, Swachhata Pledge, demonstrations on handwashing and personal hygiene, cleanliness drives in villages and school premises, and informative sessions on sanitation and environmental cleanliness. The institute also engaged in space optimisation activities that helped improve workflow efficiency and workspace aesthetics.
In addition to improving environmental hygiene, the institute responsibly discarded the scrap materials and redundant assets. Electronic waste such as obsolete computer systems, monitors, UPS units, and peripherals were also discarded. Under the Cleanliness Campaign, Over 4,000 files reviewed, nearly 1,500 cleanliness areas identified, and more than 2,000 obsolete items were responsibly disposed during the campaign.
Speaking about the campaign, Dr BS Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society) stated, “We remain committed to creating cleaner, efficient and environmentally responsible healthcare spaces. Through this coordinated effort, our staff, faculty and students contributed in creating a cleaner, clutter-free and well-managed environment.”
